text:
Laws landed for the protocol codecs; managed-module codecs still to do. Test count 431 -> 464.

ROUND TRIP (12 properties, CodecRoundTripLawSuite): jobRef, jobRefs, evidence, observation,
accounting, submission, cancellation, capabilities, logResult and logRequest on the AgentDomainJson
pairs, plus the two persisted codecs ResultEnvelopeCodec and DurableResultHandleCodec.

STRENGTH (9 tests, CodecLawStrengthSuite). This is the part that makes the round-trip laws mean
anything, and it is new machinery rather than a restatement of them. Each defaulted field is
modelled as a collapse function -- what a lossy codec returns when it forgets the field and lets the
default stand -- and the suite asserts the generator produces values the collapse changes. That is
equivalent to asserting the round-trip law would fail against such a codec, and it holds for
JobObservation.reportedCluster (the P8.A7 defect itself), .flags, .timing, EvidenceBundle.related,
AccountingBatch.missing, Diagnostic.fields and DurableResultHandle.retrySafety. Production codecs
are never mutated to run the check. The suite also verifies its own non-vacuity against a
deliberately weak generator.

Worth recording: core's existing Generators.evidenceBundle never populated "related", so it had the
same blind spot the audit described. Strengthened here.

MALFORMED plus UNKNOWN-FIELD (5, CodecMalformedInputLawSuite): 21 decoders never throw on arbitrary
JSON, on a corrupted valid encoding, or on a corrupted nested field -- every failure is a Left.
Separately, an unknown field added at any depth by a newer peer decodes to exactly the value it
would have without it, which is the unknown-field half of the parent acceptance criterion.

The first corruption corpus passed while testing nothing: mutating the sole top-level discriminator
meant no input survived as far as a field read. The non-vacuity guard that caught it is now
permanent and asserts the corpora reach full decodes as well as rejections.

BOUNDS (7, CodecBoundsLawSuite) plus the fix. decodeRemoteBoundedEvidence already bounded encoded
length before Base64.getDecoder.decode; the agent-path Decoder[BoundedEvidence]
(AgentDomainJson.scala:1750) and Decoder[LogPage] via decodeBase64 (:2125) did not. Both now use the
same ceiling the remote path uses for the same field: maximumCommandCapture for evidence,
maximumLogPage for pages. resultRefs gained a cardinality cap and shares
RemoteTaskWireLimits.MaximumBatchEntries with the two batch-element sites that were applying 100000
as a bare literal. Confirmed StructuredResultCodec.decodeBase64 already checked before allocating,
so the 2026-08-03 note was exactly right about which sites were affected.

Two rounds of guarding were needed before the bounds tests meant anything, and both failures are
worth remembering. Hand-written fixtures guessed the evidence-source shape wrong, so the oversize
assertions passed because the fixture was malformed rather than because a bound fired; fixtures are
now built by encoding a real value and substituting the field under test, and each asserts the
unmodified fixture decodes. Substituting the payload alone then violated evidence's
originalByteCount invariant, which is indistinguishable from a size rejection through isLeft and
would have passed with no bound in place at all; originalByteCount now moves with the payload and
the assertion requires the rejection message to name the limit.

BUILD: protocol's test scope now depends on core's (compile->compile;test->test) so generators are
shared. Deliberately not testkit: that artifact is published and would then carry ScalaCheck as a
compile dependency.

INCIDENTAL: SchedulerQueryResult is the only enum in its family without a derived CanEqual, so a
comparison needs a local instance. Left test-local; widening the public type's equality belongs to
the codec-ownership work on P6f.12.

REMAINING on this bead: ControlCommandJson and FileJournalControlStore.JournalCodec in the managed
module, and AgentMessageCodec envelope framing. Managed needs its own test->test wiring plus
generators for ControlCommand. Canonicalization laws are also not yet written.
